_comment: Per-install settings: everything about THIS house. Copy to config.json, or
let `node tools/setup.js` write it for you. Nothing here is about the hub
protocol — that is the same on every installation of this vendor's
controller and lives in the code.
Environment variables win over this file: PORT=3111 HUB_IP=... npm start
_televisions: LG webOS sets, driven directly rather than through the hub. The MAC is the
identity: DHCP moves the address, and a set moving between Wi-Fi and
Ethernet changes which MAC answers. Which set is in which room can only be
settled by switching one on and asking it — the console does this for you.
id must be unique and stable; it is what the API and cues address.
_goodnight: Who sleeps where. Saying "good night" puts the speaker's own room to bed:
lights and screens off, the fan and the air conditioner left running.
The key is the name the phone sends as `who` (case does not matter); the
value is a room exactly as the hub names it. Leave it out and good night is
simply not set up, which it says rather than guessing at somebody's room.
Two names can share a room, as a couple does.
_room_aliases: A second name a room answers to, for the families who call it something
other than what the installer typed. The key is the spoken name and the
value is a room exactly as the hub names it.
It is a way *in* only: every reply, the board, the guide and the history log
keep the hub's own name, so one room is never two names in the record.
An alias that would shadow a real room's name is ignored, because that would
make the room ambiguous and refuse every command to it rather than help.
_groups: A run of identical fittings around one ceiling, controlled as one tile.
Set these from the console: pick a room, pick the circuits, name it.
record_ids are the hub's own numbers, as shown beside each circuit.
_models: openai_model reads a typed or transcribed sentence. transcribe_model turns a recording into words. audio_model hears the recording directly and runs beside the transcription, so a sentence the free grammar cannot take is answered in about a second and a half instead of four; set it to "" to switch that off. It accepts wav and mp3 only, so on a box without ffmpeg the m4a a phone records falls back to the older transcribe-then-understand path on its own.
